user.title: Create a Hydronicus Plant
user.description: Set up a new Plant step by step, or import a plant file exported from another Plant. Every new Plant starts in Dry run, which calculates the real plan without controlling equipment.

menu_option_descriptions.guided: Name the Plant, choose its pump, and set up its zones from your Home Assistant areas.
menu_option_descriptions.import_plant: Rebuild a Plant, with the same entity IDs, from a plant file.

guided.title: Name the Plant
guided.description: Choose the circulation pump that the loops of every zone share. Add more pumps, shared loops, and sources later in Plant settings or through the plant file.

data_description.name: Names the Plant, its device, and its Plant-wide entities.
data_description.pump_entity: The switch that runs the circulation pump.

pump_options.name: Pump options
pump_options.description: How the pump behaves after heating demand ends.

data_description.overrun_seconds: How long the pump keeps running after heating demand ends, before the valves close. Cooling stops the pump without overrun.

zoning.title: How is your home zoned?
zoning.description: A zone is the space one thermostat controls. It covers Home Assistant areas and follows the temperature and humidity sensors that each area names in its area settings. Every answer ends in the zone form, where you choose the valves.

menu_options.zoning_whole_home: One zone for the whole home

menu_option_descriptions.zoning_whole_home: One thermostat controls the whole home, over every area that names a temperature sensor.
menu_option_descriptions.zoning_per_area: Each chosen area gets a zone and a thermostat of its own, named after the area.
menu_option_descriptions.zoning_grouped: Add zones one by one, each over the areas you group into it, such as one zone per floor.

zoning_per_area.title: Choose the areas
zoning_per_area.description: Each chosen area gets a zone of its own. The next forms add them one by one, each prefilled with its area.

data_description.areas: Starts with every area that names a temperature sensor in its area settings.

zone.title: Add a zone
zone.description: A zone has its thermostat, its areas, its sensors, and its own loop on the Plant's pump. Open Cooling to let that loop cool too.{progress}{zones}

data_description.name: Shown as the name of the zone thermostat and its entities. Leave it empty to use the name of the one chosen area, or of the floor that every chosen area is on.
data_description.areas: Home Assistant areas this zone covers. The zone follows the temperature and humidity sensors that each area names in its area settings.
data_description.temperature_sensors: Temperature sensors outside the chosen areas, such as a floor probe. A zone that Hydronicus controls needs one unless a chosen area names a temperature sensor.
data_description.external_climate_entity: Optional. When set, this climate entity owns demand for the zone, and Hydronicus only reads it and never commands it.
data_description.valves: Switches or valves of the zone's own loop. Hydronicus creates the loop and names it after the zone.
data_description.add_another: Show this form again for the next zone. Leave it off to review the Plant.

cooling.name: Cooling
cooling.description: Let the zone's own loop cool too. Cooling needs Loop valves, a humidity sensor or an area, and a supply or surface temperature sensor for condensation protection.

data_description.cooling_enabled: Enable cooling on the loop created from Loop valves. A shared loop cools only when the plant file enables it.
data_description.humidity_sensors: Humidity sensors outside the chosen areas, used for the dew point. When cooling is on, the zone needs one or an area.
data_description.supply_temperature_sensor: Sensor for the loop supply water temperature, used for condensation protection. Set this or a surface temperature sensor when cooling is on.
data_description.surface_temperature_sensor: Sensor for the floor or ceiling surface temperature, used for condensation protection. Set this or a supply temperature sensor when cooling is on.
data_description.condensation_margin: Cooling is blocked when the reference temperature comes within this margin of the dew point.

review.title: Review the Plant

data_description.confirm: Required to create a Plant that has the warnings listed above.

import_plant.title: Import a plant file
import_plant.description: Paste a plant file. Objects keep the ids the file gives them, so an exported Plant is rebuilt with the same entity IDs. The next step shows the Plant before anything is created.

data_description.document: Required. Paste the plant file in YAML, as Plant settings or the export action show it.

import_review.title: Review the imported Plant

user.title: Add a zone
user.description: A zone has its thermostat, its areas, its sensors, and the loops that heat it. Choose valves to give the zone its own loop, or choose shared loops of the Plant. Open Cooling to let the zone's own loop cool too. Saving a zone returns the Plant to Dry run.

data_description.external_climate_entity: Optional. When set, this climate entity owns demand for the zone, and Hydronicus only reads it and never commands it.
data_description.valves: Switches or valves of the zone's own loop. Hydronicus creates the loop and names it after the zone.
data_description.pump: The pump that circulates water through the zone's loop.
data_description.shared_loops: Loops of the Plant that also deliver heat to this zone. They are edited only through the plant file.

cooling.name: Cooling
cooling.description: Let the zone's own loop cool too. Cooling needs Loop valves, a humidity sensor or an area, and a supply or surface temperature sensor for condensation protection.

data_description.humidity_sensors: Humidity sensors outside the chosen areas, used for the dew point. When cooling is on, the zone needs one or an area.
data_description.supply_temperature_sensor: Sensor for the loop supply water temperature, used for condensation protection. Set this or a surface temperature sensor when cooling is on.
data_description.surface_temperature_sensor: Sensor for the floor or ceiling surface temperature, used for condensation protection. Set this or a supply temperature sensor when cooling is on.

reconfigure.description: Choose what to change in {zone}. Saving a change returns the Plant to Dry run.

zone.title: Edit zone basics
zone.description: Change the zone name, its areas, who owns its demand, its extra temperature sensors, and the shared loops that serve it. Switching to an existing climate thermostat drops the Hydronicus thermostat settings, and switching back starts from defaults.{missing_areas}

data_description.name: Shown as the name of the zone thermostat and its entities. Leave it empty to use the name of the one chosen area, or of the floor that every chosen area is on.
data_description.areas: Home Assistant areas this zone covers. The zone follows the temperature and humidity sensors that each area names in its area settings.
data_description.temperature_sensors: Temperature sensors outside the chosen areas, such as a floor probe. A zone that Hydronicus controls needs one unless a chosen area names a temperature sensor.
data_description.external_climate_entity: Optional. When set, this climate entity owns demand for the zone, and Hydronicus only reads it and never commands it.
data_description.shared_loops: Loops of the Plant that also deliver heat to this zone. They are edited only through the plant file.

thermostat.title: Edit thermostat settings
thermostat.description: Configure how the Hydronicus thermostat of this zone turns demand on and off.

data_description.heating_start_delta: Heating starts when the zone temperature falls this far below the target.
data_description.heating_stop_delta: Heating stops when the zone temperature rises this far above the target.
data_description.minimum_active_duration_seconds: Once demand starts, it is held for at least this long. Use 0 to disable.
data_description.minimum_idle_duration_seconds: Once demand stops, it stays off for at least this long. Use 0 to disable.
data_description.comfort: Optional target temperature for the comfort preset.
data_description.eco: Optional target temperature for the eco preset.
data_description.away: Optional target temperature for the away preset.

cooling.name: Cooling
cooling.description: Hysteresis used when the zone is in cooling mode.

data_description.cooling_start_delta: Cooling starts when the zone temperature rises this far above the target.
data_description.cooling_stop_delta: Cooling stops when the zone temperature falls this far below the target.

sensors.title: Edit sensors
sensors.description: Choose the areas the zone covers, the humidity sensors it uses besides them, and how temperature readings are combined.{missing_areas}

data_description.areas: Home Assistant areas this zone covers. The zone follows the temperature and humidity sensors that each area names in its area settings.
data_description.temperature_aggregation: How the readings of the extra temperature sensors and the areas are combined into one zone temperature.
data_description.humidity_sensors: Optional humidity sensors outside the chosen areas, used for the dew point when cooling.
data_description.configure_sensor_metadata: Opens one extra form per extra temperature sensor, then one per area, to set weights, freshness limits, and the designated reference.

sensor_metadata.title: Edit temperature sensor
sensor_metadata.description: Configure {sensor} explicitly. A required sensor blocks the zone when stale or unavailable. Weighted mean is available only after every selected sensor has this editable path.

data_description.sensor_entity: The sensor these settings apply to.
data_description.required: A required sensor that is stale or unavailable blocks the zone. An optional one is left out of the aggregate instead.
data_description.weight: Relative weight of this sensor in the weighted mean.
data_description.calibration_offset: Added to every reading from this sensor before aggregation.
data_description.max_age_seconds: A reading older than this is treated as stale.
data_description.designated_reference: Used alone when the zone aggregation is set to designated reference.

area_metadata.title: Edit area settings

data_description.required: A required temperature sensor that is stale or unavailable blocks the zone. An optional one, the default for an area, is left out of the aggregate instead.
data_description.weight: Relative weight of this area's temperature in the weighted mean.
data_description.max_age_seconds: A reading older than this is treated as stale.
data_description.designated_reference: This area's temperature is used alone when the zone aggregation is set to designated reference.

sensor_policy.title: Choose sensor aggregation
sensor_policy.description: Every extra temperature sensor and area has editable settings, so every aggregation policy is available.

data_description.temperature_aggregation: How the readings of the extra temperature sensors and the areas are combined into one zone temperature.

edit_loop.title: Choose a loop
edit_loop.description: Choose the loop of this zone to edit or remove.

data_description.loop: One of the loops that belong to this zone.

loop.title: Configure a loop
loop.description: A loop of {zone} is a water path through its valves and one pump. Every chosen valve must open before the pump may run.

data_description.name: Shown as the name of this loop.
data_description.valves: Switches or valves that belong to this zone. A new entity becomes a new valve, and a removed one is deleted unless another loop of the zone still uses it.
data_description.shared_valves: Valves of the Plant that this loop also needs open. They are edited only through the plant file.
data_description.pump: The pump that circulates water through this loop.
data_description.valve_opening_time_seconds: How long this loop's zone valves need to open before the pump may start.
data_description.configure_valve_feedback: Opens one extra form per zone valve of this loop to set its readiness and position feedback.
data_description.remove_loop: Removes the loop, and the zone valves that no other loop of the zone uses.

cooling.name: Cooling
cooling.description: Enable cooling and configure condensation protection for this loop.

data_description.cooling_enabled: Allow this loop to deliver cooling. Cooling requires a supply or surface temperature reference.
data_description.supply_temperature_sensor: Sensor for the loop supply water temperature, used for condensation protection.
data_description.surface_temperature_sensor: Sensor for the floor or ceiling surface temperature, used for condensation protection.
data_description.condensation_margin: Cooling is blocked when the reference temperature comes within this margin of the dew point.
data_description.supply_temperature_max_age_seconds: A supply temperature reading older than this is treated as stale.
data_description.surface_temperature_max_age_seconds: A surface temperature reading older than this is treated as stale.

valve_details.title: Edit valve feedback
valve_details.description: Optional entities that confirm what {valve} ({entity}) is doing.

data_description.readiness_entity_id: Optional entity that reports the valve is fully open. When set, the pump waits for it.
data_description.position_feedback_entity: Optional sensor that reports the measured valve position.
data_description.position_feedback_max_age_seconds: Position feedback older than this is treated as stale.

dry_run.title: Dry run
dry_run.description: Dry run calculates the real heating and cooling plan without service calls. Turn it off only after reviewing the configured outputs.

data_description.dry_run: When on, Hydronicus calculates the full plan but sends no commands to any actuator.

dry_run_confirmation.description:
Hydronicus will be allowed to control only these exact heating and cooling outputs when the plan permits them:
{outputs}

data_description.overrun_seconds: How long the pump keeps running after heating demand ends, before the valves close. Cooling stops the pump without overrun.

missing_sensor_binding.title: Missing sensor for {object_name}
missing_sensor_binding.description: In Plant {plant}, the {binding} is missing or renamed, so the heating or cooling path that depends on it is blocked. {object_name} is Plant equipment that only the plant file edits: open the Plant settings, choose Edit plant file, change the binding, and apply the file. Alternatively, restore the sensor: re-enable or reconnect the device or integration that provides it, or give its replacement the original entity ID in the entity settings. The repair clears automatically as soon as the entity is available again.

confirm.title: Missing sensor for {object_name}
confirm.description: In Plant {plant}, the {binding} is missing or renamed, so the heating or cooling path that depends on it is blocked. Select Submit to edit {owner}, choose the current sensor, and save. Restoring the original entity also works; the repair clears automatically as soon as the binding resolves.

abort.reconfigure_subentry: {owner} is open for editing. The repair clears after a valid sensor is saved for {object_name}.
abort.subentry_not_found: The zone or source that owned this binding no longer exists. If a binding is still unresolved, a new repair appears.

Restoring the original entity also works; the repair clears automatically as soon as the binding resolves.

abort.subentry_not_found: The zone or source that owned this binding no longer exists. If a binding is still unresolved, a new repair appears.

missing_area_sensor_binding.title: {plant}, zone {object_name}: missing {sensor} of area {area}
missing_area_sensor_binding.description: In Plant {plant}, zone {object_name} follows the sensors of area {area}, and the {sensor} that the area names is missing or renamed. Renaming an entity does not update the area, so open the settings of area {area}, choose the current sensor, and save. The repair clears automatically as soon as the sensor is available again.

zone_area_missing.title: {plant}, zone {zone}: missing area {area}
zone_area_missing.description: In Plant {plant}, zone {zone} covers area {area}, which no longer exists in Home Assistant, so the zone gets no reading from it. Remove the area from the zone, or create an area named {recreate_name} again: Home Assistant makes a new area's ID from its name, and that name gives the ID {area_id} that the zone covers. You can rename the area afterwards. The repair clears automatically once the zone no longer covers a missing area.

confirm.title: {plant}, zone {zone}: missing area {area}
confirm.description: In Plant {plant}, zone {zone} covers area {area}, which no longer exists in Home Assistant, so the zone gets no reading from it. Select Submit to edit {owner} and remove the area. Creating an area named {recreate_name} again also works, because that name gives the ID {area_id} that the zone covers; the repair clears automatically once the zone no longer covers a missing area.

abort.reconfigure_subentry: {owner} is open for editing. The repair clears after the zone is saved without the missing area.
abort.subentry_not_found: The zone that covered this area no longer exists. If another zone still covers a missing area, a new repair appears.

zone_without_temperature_source.title: {plant}, zone {zone}: no temperature sensor
zone_without_temperature_source.description: In Plant {plant}, zone {zone} covers {areas}, but the area settings name no temperature sensor that Hydronicus can follow, so the zone is blocked and does not heat or cool. Choose a temperature sensor in the area settings, or add a temperature sensor to the zone. The repair clears automatically once the zone has a temperature sensor.

confirm.title: {plant}, zone {zone}: no temperature sensor
confirm.description: In Plant {plant}, zone {zone} covers {areas}, but the area settings name no temperature sensor that Hydronicus can follow, so the zone is blocked and does not heat or cool. Select Submit to edit {owner} and add a temperature sensor or another area. Choosing a temperature sensor in the area settings also works; the repair clears automatically once the zone has a temperature sensor.

abort.reconfigure_subentry: {owner} is open for editing. The repair clears once the zone has a temperature sensor.
abort.subentry_not_found: The zone no longer exists. If another zone has no temperature sensor, a new repair appears.

zone_area_self_feed.title: {plant}, zone {zone}: area {area} names a Hydronicus sensor
zone_area_self_feed.description: In Plant {plant}, zone {zone} covers area {area}, whose settings name {entity_ids}. Hydronicus provides that sensor, and following it would feed the Plant back into itself, so zone {zone} ignores it. Open the settings of area {area} and choose a sensor that measures the room. The repair clears automatically once the area names another sensor.

output_conflict.title: {plant} is held in Dry run
output_conflict.description: {plant} is set to run outside Dry run, but {other_plant} is already out of Dry run and controls {entities}. Two live Plants would fight over these entities, so Hydronicus holds {plant} in Dry run because {other_plant} is using the same outputs, and sends no commands from it. Its Dry run setting and confirmed outputs are kept. {plant} resumes automatically when the conflict is gone, for example when {other_plant} enters Dry run, is unloaded, or is removed. To end the conflict for good, bind different entities in one of the Plants, remove one of the Plants, or turn on Dry run for one of them.
